Inspect effective supported SDK/logger enablement, minimum severity and trace filters. Keep optional native/direct-OTel cost guards separate from pipeline ownership. Default enabled is SHOULD true, not MUST.

Collector processing can satisfy an approved downstream boundary. It cannot close forbidden pre-SDK/pre-writer capture; the existing stricter privacy rule was already present. No weakening of that rule.
Selected semantic EventName cannot contain per-occurrence identifiers; only permitted varying data goes in attributes. Ordinary bridged messages need no EventName.
Distinguish server throttle instructions from client backoff under one whole deadline; verify supported exporter behavior instead of adding an app retry loop. HTTP400 is non-retryable.
When the selected supported Emit API derives exception fields, user attributes win. Do not add an optional API or raw exception capture solely for this test.
A selected event-to-span processor must continue the record; its absence does not require adding a new processor.
Only an owned custom asynchronous processor needs a verified safe snapshot/clone of mutable records. Built-in processors need no replacement; unknown public support stays unverified.
Development recommendation against instrumentation-generated artificial status exceptions excludes logging bridges and does not ban intentional application error logs.
Inspect SDK discard diagnostics: at most one per record, not one per dropped attribute. Do not replace SDK internals.
Preserve scope identity; conflicting scope attributes on the same logger are not new per-record fields.
No syslog sink is selected. RFC5424-specific formatting is conditional on that path and does not belong in every language setup.
An effective supported SDK_DISABLED opt-out is distinct from a missing bridge and does not disable an original native sink. A flat setting ignored by a file loader is not effective.

For selected instrumentation exception events, require the permitted identifiable type/message pairing. If policy forbids both, report the semantic limitation without capturing them. Do not impose the floor on ordinary bridge messages.
Check exception.escaped deprecation and actual version/compatibility policy. A deprecated span attribute is not a reason to delete approved fields or migrate ordinary bridges.
Record supported transport request/response size limits separately from attributes and Body. No universal new application Body cap or unsupported SDK option.
Batch guidance previously unqualified. An operator-owned SDK console exporter can legitimately pair a simple processor; BLRP settings then do not apply and synchronous cost is the relevant check.

The existing instruction expresses preservation policy for newly added defaults; it never promised that env always overrides code. State standard code-over-env resource merge explicitly and avoid conflicting new code keys. Check malformed env and actual effective resource.
Reuse existing semconv keys; custom application/company names avoid namespace collisions and new otel.* names need spec approval. A recommendation is not an unconditional new-prefix mandate.
An existing selected _ref path uses a registry-defined base and string reference, preferably absolute URI. No new storage or permission to capture forbidden content. Absence is not a gap.

Inspect selected log.iostream/original/uid with Development status. Bound original content before construction; distinguishable records cannot share UID. A trace ID is not a record UID; absent UID is valid.
Call-site conventions must match the verified bridge version. Source/SDK migration is not justified merely because a newer registry has dotted keys.
Use implemented SDK log metrics at their documented stage; processed/created do not prove receiver acceptance. No duplicate app metrics or assumed unsupported instruments.
Record language Logs signal maturity as well as per-feature stability/version. Development/RC status does not justify skipping a supported stack or upgrading it.
No HEC log sink selected. The appendix is non-normative and cannot create a mandatory application requirement from Splunk branding.
